questions.text: Why does a video diffusion model couple information across frames instead of generating each frame independently with an image model?

options.A: To eliminate the need for spatial compression of high-resolution frames.
options.B: To guarantee physically correct motion for arbitrarily long clips.
options.C: To model temporal relationships and reduce inconsistent appearance across frames.
options.D: To replace denoising with exact likelihood evaluation of each frame.

questions.explanation: Cross-frame coupling lets the model learn motion and preserve related content across time. Independent image generation lacks those dependencies and can flicker. Coupling does not guarantee physics or eliminate compression and denoising.

questions.text: Full attention over all spatiotemporal patches exceeds your video model's memory budget. Which change reduces attention cost while retaining spatial and temporal interactions?

options.A: Replace all temporal position embeddings with the same constant.
options.B: Generate each frame independently and discard cross-frame interactions.
options.C: Increase the number of patches by reducing every patch dimension.
options.D: Factorize attention into within-frame spatial and across-frame temporal passes.

questions.explanation: Factorized attention separates within-frame spatial attention from temporal attention across frames, reducing the cost relative to full attention over every spatiotemporal token pair while retaining both kinds of interaction.

questions.text: This diagnostic measures mean absolute frame-to-frame change. What does it print?
questions.explanation: The smooth sequence has three absolute deltas of 1, averaging 1. The flickery sequence has three absolute deltas of 3, averaging 3. This diagnostic measures changes, not semantic correctness or motion quality by itself.
